title: Streamline console response merging and cache coherency
creator: Anya Patel
description: Background: The Console backend has multiple code paths that perform overlapping aggregation work for dashboard and route-level APIs: a set of GraphQL resolvers, several Express REST handlers, and a small aggregation service used by the notifications dashboard. These layers have diverged (duplicate joins, per-request materialization, and slightly different caching policies). Symptoms: increased p95 latency on high-concurrency pages, cache thrashing, and inconsistent stale reads between the GraphQL API and the REST endpoints (users report different counts in /api/usage vs. dashboards). Goal: consolidate response-merging logic into a single, well-instrumented middleware, standardize cache coherency rules, and upgrade the in-process caching library to a production-maintainable implementation. Scope: (1) introduce a shared response-composition middleware used by both GraphQL resolvers and REST handlers, (2) replace ad-hoc per-handler memoization with lru-cache v8 and a read-through backend backed by Redis for heavy keys, (3) add request fingerprinting and singleflight stamping to avoid duplicate upstream work, (4) expose route-level cache TTL controls via Console config and a feature flag for gradual rollout. Non-goals: complete rewrite of the aggregation service or migration to a separate microservice—this is a cleanup/refactor to reduce duplication and improve latency in the current runtime.
acceptance_criteria: Shared response-composition middleware exists and is used by at least: /api/dashboard/summary, /graphql:DashboardSummary resolver, and /api/usage
p95 latency for the Dashboard summary route reduced by >= 40% under the standard sim load (baseline: 420ms -> target <= 250ms),
Cache coherency: repeated reads after a write within 5s observe consistent counts across GraphQL and REST endpoints in 99% of tests
No behavior regressions: integration test suite for Console endpoints passes, and canary rollout shows no increase in error budget for 48 hours
Instrumentation: metrics for cache hit/miss, stampede prevention events, and average response-merge time are emitted to prod telemetry with dashboards linked in the ticket
notes: Investigated current codepaths: src/services/aggregator/*, src/graphql/resolvers/dashboard.ts, src/routes/dashboard.ts — found 3 slightly different join implementations
Proposed libraries: lru-cache v8 (in-process), node-singleflight (to dedupe concurrent upstream calls), Redis as read-through for hot keys
Feature flag plan: enable 'response_merge_v2' for 5% of users -> 25% -> 100% with rollback strategy tied to error budget and p95 spike detection
Instrumentation: add Prometheus metrics: console.response_merge.ms, console.response_merge.cache_hit, console.response_merge.stampede_dedupe
Upgrade notes: bump lru-cache from 6.x to 8.x; run compatibility test for TypeScript types and Node 18 runtime—small API changes expected for 'ttl' semantics
